entry.content:
In 1969, Mercedes-Benz refused to sell its C 111, even to buyers offering blank checks, and again refused when the C 111-II arrived months later. This C 111-II has gullwing doors and a mid-mounted four-rotor rotary engine that makes 350 horsepower and revs to 9,000 rpm. Metallic orange paint covers the body, and the interior is trimmed with houndstooth. Chassis 33 appeared in Playboy's first German issue, and Herbert von Karajan, who conducted the Berlin Philharmonic, drove it. After almost 20 years on display at the company museum, Mercedes F1 driver George Russell drove it into Silverstone for a practice day. The car is now up for auction, the first C 111 a private buyer can bid on.

Inspired by the character of the British countryside, REISS' Fall 2026 menswear collection brings a modern edge to heritage dressing. Standout pieces include the tobacco-brown Bodrum distressed shearling aviator jacket, Kingsley speckled wool overshirt, Vatali open-collar wool-cotton jumper, Tuscan houndstooth blazer, and Deal wool pinstripe trousers. Rich textures, traditional fabrics, and a palette of warm neutrals, earthy browns, and deep berry tones give the collection its seasonal character, balancing relaxed layering with considered tailoring. The result is a versatile wardrobe that moves effortlessly between country escapes and city streets.

entry.content:
Ferrari drops the hybrid system for two new 296s that use only a twin-turbo V6, one for the road and one for the racetrack. Both weigh about 300 pounds less than the hybrid 296 GTB. The 296 Challenge Stradale, the street-legal one, makes 670 horsepower, and its rear wing, front splitter and vortex generators press it down at speed with 72 percent more downforce than the GTB. The 296 Challenge Evo is built for Ferrari's one-make race series and makes 700 horsepower, and it laps Italy's Mugello circuit eight-tenths of a second quicker than the earlier 296 Challenge.

entry.content:
Go beyond basic weight tracking with the RENPHO MorphoScan Nova, a smart body composition scale designed to deliver a more complete picture of fitness progress. Using eight-electrode hand and foot sensors with dual-frequency technology, it measures more than 50 body metrics, including segmental muscle mass and body fat, helping users better understand changes across different areas of the body. A built-in 4.3-inch TFT handle display puts results and progress trends front and center without requiring a phone after every scan, while guided measurements and the RENPHO Health app make long-term tracking straightforward. Compatible with Apple Health, Google Fit, and MyFitnessPal, it supports unlimited user profiles, a 400-pound capacity, USB-C charging, and up to 150 days of battery life. FSA/HSA eligible, it's a more insightful upgrade to the everyday bathroom scale.

entry.content:
